# The Lost Honey Trail

In Whisperwood Forest, where the morning mist hung low and familiar, Oliver the Bear woke to find his honey supply missing.

"That's not right," he muttered, shuffling out of his den. Routine matters, and losing his honey meant disrupting his whole week.

He met Meadow the Rabbit hopping along the old path. "Same thing happened to me—my carrots vanished!"

They gathered old friends: Basil the Owl, who knew every tree, and Dot the Squirrel, who remembered every path. This was the way problems got solved—people working together, not complicated schemes.

The trail led them past the Great Oak, the same one their grandparents had spoken of. Something felt different though. The flowers along the path glowed faintly.

"I don't like this," Oliver admitted. "I prefer knowing what I'm walking into."

"Stick together," Meadow said. "That's what matters."

They discovered young Chip the Raccoon, new to the forest, had taken the food. He'd been too embarrassed to ask for help finding his own supplies. The animals could have gotten angry—they didn't. Oliver remembered being new once. It wasn't comfortable.

"Show us your den," Basil said. "We'll help you learn the good spots."

Together they spent the afternoon teaching Chip where the sweetest berries grew and which trees held the best nuts. Chip shared stories about his old forest home.

By evening, Oliver returned with honey from the shared harvest—less than his usual amount, but enough. More importantly, the forest felt right again. Sometimes routine needed a small adjustment, not a complete change.

"Good help matters," he thought, curling into his den. "Always has."

The adventure wasn't grand, but it worked. That was enough.
